problems: rule falsely says every sentence needs am/is/are (sentences with an action verb do not)

fix.rule: A sentence with no action word needs am, is or are: I am, he/she/it is, you/we/they are.

problems: his = a man / her = a woman leaves out boys and girls (child learners, e.g. Lina, Omar)

fix.rule: Pick by the owner: his (boy, man), her (girl, woman), their (more than one), plus my, your, our.

problems: interleaving item ambiguous: 'The cat is on the box' is also correct

fix.interleaving_item: Write in or on: The cat is ___ the box. It is hiding inside. -> answer: in

problems: 'the noun after a number takes -s' is false for one (one duck)

fix.rule: Say there is for one thing and there are for two or more; then the noun takes -s.

problems: rule does not cover place or time at the end, which the outcome requires ('then the rest' is vague)

fix.rule: Put who first, then the action, then what, then place or time; describing words go before nouns.

problems: usual error (one long line joined with and) is not what the wrong sentence shows

fix.usual_error: no capital at the start, a small i for I, or no full stop at the end

problems: rule says 'add -ed' for every past action (not true for irregular verbs) and does not match the -d / -ied examples

fix.rule: For a finished past action, most verbs add -ed (walked, moved, carried), even with yesterday.

problems: interleaving answer 'an' is not one of the offered choices (a or some)

fix.interleaving_item: Write a, an or some: The horse wants ___ apple. -> answer: an

fix.rule: We eat food, and we eat soup too; we drink water, juice and milk.
fix.usual_error: drink soup instead of eat soup
fix.word_set: bread, rice, apple, milk, egg, fish, soup, water, juice, tea, cheese, chicken, banana, eat, drink

problems: rule mentions v/f but no word in the set has v; 'bag' is a confusing example of p
'rubber' has an adult meaning in US English

fix.rule: Classroom things have short English names; write p, not b: pen, pencil, paper.
fix.usual_error: b for p (ben, bencil), or an Arabic phrase word for word
fix.worked_examples: [eraser] The robot has an eraser. | [scissors] The robot cuts paper with scissors.
fix.word_set: desk, chair, pen, pencil, book, board, bag, ruler, eraser, marker, notebook, scissors

problems: usual error says v for f but the wrong form shows f for v (sefen)

fix.usual_error: f and v mixed up in a number (fivteen, sefen), or clock for hour

problems: wrong sentence 'little big' is not the named usual error (wrong partner of a pair)
word set has kind, funny, friendly (personality, not hair/eyes/height)
clue 'not fat' is body-shaming risk for children

fix.word_set: hair, eyes, nose, big, tall, short, long, curly, straight, thin, black, brown, blonde, blue, green, grey

problems: rule (make = new things) does not explain the real confusion 'make a mistake'

fix.rule: We make new things (a cake, a plan) and a mistake; we do jobs and tasks (homework, the dishes).
